Cmcm structure and fractional coordinates at 121 GPa and 300 K: Murakami et al., Science 304, 855-858 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1095932, ICSD 158959. The measured 121 GPa cell (a=2.456, b=8.042, c=6.093 A) was isotropically expanded to the Mosenfelder V0=162.2 A^3 while preserving its axial ratios, so Dioptas' isotropic EoS scaling returns a close approximation to the measured high-pressure cell. Phase-line intensities were calculated from the cited structure using independent-atom X-ray form factors.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Debye temperature law:** integrated\_gruneisen
- **Thermal pressure reference:** reference\_isentrope

</details>

Global errors-in-variables inversion of 48 Guignot et al. static P-V-T observations and six PPv shock P-density states. V0=162.2 A^3 was fixed. Table 4 reports K0S=225(2) GPa, K0S'=4.21(7), theta0=990(146) K, gamma0=2.61(67), q=2.1(8), and Cvm=1.035(50) J g^-1 K^-1; Cvmax is the exact molar conversion using 100.3875 g mol^-1. The BM3 term is a 300 K reference isentrope, so thermal pressure subtracts energy at T\_S(V)=Tr\*theta(V)/theta0. The three source-reported shock temperatures are retained as measured diagnostics but are not constraints in the solid PPv inversion; section 3 explicitly identifies shock-temperature fitting only for MgSiO3 liquid.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

Experimental BM3 fit 1 to laser-heated DAC data from this study plus Guignot et al., reaching 265 GPa. Stored as a room-temperature cold curve only because the published thermal fit uses an Al'tshuler gamma(V) function not implemented by Dioptas. Sakai et al. prefer their Keane fit for multi-megabar extrapolation; the BM3 parameters are strongly correlated and should be used within the experimental range rather than extrapolated.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

    - **Classification:** parity

        - **K0:** 237.18599457

- **Reported inconsistencies:** Figure 2 captions the Anderson curve as K0=236(1) GPa, while the abstract, Results prose, and Table 3 report 237(1) GPa. The repeated prose/table value is stored; the caption-only value is not added as a duplicate EOS.; Results prose says Z=2, whereas the Table 1 note explicitly says Cmcm Z=4 and the listed conventional-cell sites have multiplicities 4, 4, 4, and 8. Peritheos uses the conventional Cmcm cell and Z=4; Z=2 is consistent only with a primitive-cell count.; Table 2 prints MgSiO3 a=2.250(3) A in row 3, inconsistent with b, c, and V=120.11(22) A^3; a near 2.450 A would be required. The printed 2.250 value is preserved, and EOS reproduction uses the independently printed volume.
- **Unresolved issues:** The article does not state the confidence convention of the parenthetical K0 errors and publishes no parameter covariance matrix.; The exact weighted-least-squares objective and weights used by the cited Angel (2000) program are not printed.; The fixed 162.86 A^3 zero-pressure volume was adopted from a 0 K LDA calculation even though the experimental isotherm and reported K0 are at 300 K.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Abstract; Experimental methods; Results and printed EOS equation; Tables 1-3; Figure 2 and caption.
- **Equation:** Journal page 476: the printed third-order Birch-Murnaghan equation uses x=(V/V0)^(1/3), with P=(3/2)K0(x^-7-x^-5)\[1+(3/4)(K0\_prime-4)(x^-2-1)\]. Fixing K0\_prime=4 makes the executable curve exactly BM2.
- **V0:** Journal page 477 and Table 3: 162.86 A^3, fixed; adopted from the 0 K LDA calculation of Oganov and Ono (2004), not measured at ambient pressure.
- **K0:** Results prose and Table 3, journal page 477: 237(1) GPa for pressures reduced with the Anderson et al. (1989) gold standard.
- **K0 prime:** Results prose and Table 3, journal page 477: fixed at 4; represented implicitly by BM2 rather than as a fitted parameter.
- **Reference state:** The fit is described as a 300 K isothermal EOS with a zero-pressure V0 and K0, extrapolated from 116.1-144.4 GPa data. V0 itself was adopted from a 0 K LDA calculation.
- **Fit selection and weighting:** Experimental methods and Results: all six Table 2 P-V observations were used in a weighted least-squares fit with the method cited to Angel (2000); the article does not publish the exact objective or covariance matrix.
- **Uncertainties:** Table 3 gives K0 as 237(1) GPa but does not identify the confidence convention. V0 and K0\_prime were fixed. Numerical parameter covariance is not published.

</details>

V0=163.813 A3 is adopted from Tsuchiya et al. (2004), not measured at ambient conditions. K0'=4 is fixed. K0 is first fitted to three 300 K points, then held fixed for the thermal fit to all 21 PPv observations on the original Speziale-MgO scale. alpha(T)=alpha0+alpha1\*T with alpha(300)=1.7e-5 K^-1 imposed, so alpha0=1.7e-5-300\*alpha1 is dependent. The record preserves the independently rounded Table 2 coefficients, whose alpha(300)=1.7009e-5 differs slightly from the exact constraint. The Pv-only row is excluded; the companion Pv fit also requires Funamori et al. data and is not claimed reproduced. Unweighted pressure residuals reproduce the free coefficients within printed errors; the source does not supply a complete optimizer/weighting protocol or covariance. Published coefficients are retained; this non-default record does not replace the Dorogokupets synthesis.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

Flyer velocity, initial density, shock transit velocity, and the three populated pyrometric temperatures are measured; particle velocity, pressure, and shocked density are derived by impedance matching and Rankine-Hugoniot relations; phase\_state is interpreted. Parenthesized values are retained as generic published uncertainties because the table does not specify their statistic. Five rows originate in Akins and Luo; the 245.4 GPa aggregate experiment is new in this paper.
